1  Mr. Vincent Marki, Advocate  ------
Order No. 06 / Dated : 04.12.2025.
1.

Insurance-Company is in appeal against the judgment and award of compensation under Section 166 of the M.V. Act in Title (M.V.) Suit No. 65 of 2015, whereby and whereunder, a finding of contributory negligence has been recorded with respect to the vehicle under its insurance cover and liability has been fixed on it to pay part of the compensation amount.
2. Facts are not in dispute or challenge before this Court that on 14.06.2013 2025:JHHC:36647 Upendra Yadav, who was cleaner of truck bearing registration no. JH 12C 3442, died in a motor vehicle accident involving another truck bearing registration no. JH 20A 6971.
3.
The judgment and award of compensation is under challenge mainly on three grounds.

Firstly, it is argued that learned Tribunal has recorded a finding of contributory negligence 50:50,
whereas it was the truck bearing registration no. JH 20A 6971 which was responsible for the accident.

Secondly, it is argued that learned Tribunal erred in taking 1/4th deduction in living and personal expenses of the deceased, as during the pendency of the motor vehicle suit, Basudeo Mahto, father of the deceased, had died on 23.03.2019 during the pendency of the claim case,
reducing the legal dependents to three, for which 1/3rd will be applicable for deducting the personal living expenses of the deceased.

Thirdly, it is contended that the award of Rs.1,00,000/- under the heading of 'love and affection' is not in accord with ratio laid down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi {(2017) 16 SCC 680}.
4.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi {(2017) 16 SCC 680}
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no. 6 as well as the claimants have defended the impugned order.

It is submitted, and rightly so, that there is no contrary evidence to show that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the truck bearing registration no. JH 20A 6971.
5.
The FIR (Ext.1) was lodged against the driver of both the vehicles and charge-sheet (Ext.2) was also submitted against the driver of both the vehicles.
Under the circumstances, I do not find any reason to interfere with the findings of the learned Tribunal regarding contributory negligence on the part of the driver of both the vehicles.

6. There is, however, merit in the submissions advanced that since one of the claimants namely,
Basudeo Mahto, had died during the pendency of the suit, therefore, the deduction for personal and living expenses will be 1/3rd and the consortium will be admissible as per the ratio laid down by the in Pranay Sethi case (supra).
7.

It is difficult to concede the argument advanced on behalf of the claimants that since Basudeo Mahto was alive when the accident took place and died 2025:JHHC:36647 four years thereafter,
National Insurance Company Limited vs Anjani Devi on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7789339/
2 therefore, personal living expense has to be deducted as 1/4th.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deduction has to proceed as per the dependency and once there is change in dependency, the deductions will follow accordingly.
8. Under the circumstances, this Court is of the view that 1/3 rd deduction will be applicable and not 1/4th.
Further, the compensation under the non- conventional head will be admissible as per the ratio down by the Apex Court in Pranay Sethi case (supra).

9. Taking Rs. 6500/- as monthly income, 1/3rd as deduction on personal and living expense, 40% as future prospect and multiplier of 18, the final compensation will work out as under: -
 Annual Income = Rs.6500/- X 12 Rs.78,000/-
 Future Prospect Rs.78,000/- Rs. 31,200 /-
 X 40%
 After adding annual income and Rs. 78,000+Rs.31,200  future prospect =Rs.1,09,200 /-
 Deduction of 1/3rd personal and living Rs. 36,400/-
 expense  Multiplier of 18 Rs. 72,800X 18/-
 Conventional Head Rs.77,000/-
 Total Rs.13.10,400 /- + Rs. 77,000  =Rs.13,87,400 /-
10.Since it is a case of contributory negligence, and the lability to pay compensation will be 50%
each on both the Insurance Company, therefore the Appellant Insurance Company is directed to make payment of Rs. 13,87,400/- with interest @ 7.5% from the date of filing of the claim application, within a month of the order, which shall be disbursed to the claimants by the Tribunal on terms fixed by it.
Interest on the compensation amount paid under the head of future prospect will not be admissible in view of the ratio laid down in M.A. No. 386 of 2025 dated 18.11.2025.
Miscellaneous Appeal is disposed of.
Pending I.A., if any, also stands disposed of.
Statutory amount deposited at the time of preferring the instant Misc. Appeal be remitted to the Tribunal to be disbursed along with compensation to the claimant within a month of this order.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Pawan/ -
